newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent trades sideways, looking for mogas lead.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent trades sideways, looking for mogas lead.

text.p: IPE Brent crude was marginally lower but within a sideways range on Wednesday after strong gains on Tuesday. Gas oil built upon yesterday's strength.
August Brent, which expires later today was off six cents at $18.33 at 0945 GMT, but most market attention was directed at September which was down two cents at $18.35.
Dealers said Brent had upside potential if gasoline took up the energy complex baton as was seen yesterday.
September Brent faces initial support at $18.30 and $18.18.
"I see it at neutral at $18.18, but below this shows weakness has returned," said one broker.
Rolling August into September started earlier than usual and was well underway, dealers said.
Bullish API data helped spur the market higher, but some analysts said this news was now done.
"The APIs were expected to be bullish and they were, but what's new now to push the market?," questioned one trader.
Dealers said crude had failed to break resistance yesterday around $18.45 although NYMEX gasoline did.
IPE gas oil was $1.25 firmer on August at $164.00 a tonne in a catch-up play to crude's late gains. Dealers said gas oil was looking neutral and facing stiff resistance around $165.25.
Brokers saw 60.10 cents a gallon on NYMEX gasoline as a break-higher point.

Iraq may be allowed to carry over only five percent of its $1 billion quarterly limit for oil sales in to the second tranche of exports suggested Baghdad may be forced to sell 1.5 million barrels a day (bpd), assuming sales beginning in the last week of July compared, with about 660,000 bpd in the December 10, 1996 to June 7, 1997 period.
